issues.title: Exit command resolves after activity termination
issues.description: The exit command calls `activity.finish()` before `invoke.resolve()`. This creates a race condition where the activity lifecycle may terminate before the JavaScript callback receives the resolution response. This can lead to lost responses, potential crashes in the JavaScript layer when expecting a resolution that never arrives, and unreliable exit behavior. The resolution should occur before finishing the activity to ensure the response is sent back to the frontend before the Android activity is destroyed.

issues.title: Back navigation handled by both framework and plugin
issues.description: Setting `handleBackNavigation` to `true` in TauriActivity causes the Wry framework to handle back navigation, which conflicts with the AppPlugin's custom OnBackPressedCallback implementation. This creates competing back button handlers where both the framework's default behavior and the plugin's custom logic attempt to process back button events. This can result in double back navigation, skipped history entries, or inconsistent behavior when users press the back button. The value should remain `false` to allow the AppPlugin to be the sole handler of back button events as designed in the PR.

issues.title: Exit command not registered in build.rs permissions
issues.description: The Android exit command is implemented in AppPlugin.kt but is not registered in the Rust build.rs file under the core:app plugin commands list. Without registration in the PLUGINS constant, the exit command will not be accessible through the Tauri IPC bridge, making the exit functionality completely non-functional. All Tauri commands must be registered in build.rs to be callable from the frontend, as evidenced by the pattern used for register_listener and remove_listener commands which were properly added to the same list.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #14133 - feat(core): back button event on Android, closes #8142

structured_output.summary:
This PR adds an Android `AppPlugin` (Kotlin). It registers an `OnBackPressedCallback`. With no JS listener, the callback goes back in the webview's history or falls through to the activity's default behaviour. With a listener, it sends a `back-button` event carrying `canGoBack`. On the Rust side, the core `app` plugin's `setup` now registers this Android plugin, and `register_listener`/`remove_listener` permissions are added to the app plugin's defaults. On the JS side, `onBackButtonPress` is exported from `@tauri-apps/api/app`. The wry version goes from 0.53.2 to 0.53.4 to pick up `WryActivity.handleBackNavigation`.

The design follows the Capacitor reference closely, but two problems block merging. First, the Android `setup` block doesn't compile: `PluginHandle` implements `Clone` but not `Copy`, so `*handle_ref` tries to move out of a shared reference. CI never caught it because the block is gated behind `cfg(target_os = "android")`. Second, `TauriActivity` sets `handleBackNavigation = true`. That keeps wry's built-in back handling on, which defeats the point of routing back presses through `AppPlugin`. It should almost certainly be `false`. There are also smaller gaps. If the page reloads, old listeners stay registered and the back button stops responding. And the `exit` command can't be reached from JS, so once an app adds a listener it has no built-in way to close itself.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The Android-only Rust setup code fails to compile (a move out of `&PluginHandle`). On top of that, `handleBackNavigation = true` leaves wry's own back handling running alongside AppPlugin, which most likely undermines the new feature.

architecture.overview:
Tauri's Android shell is a `TauriActivity` that extends wry's `WryActivity`. Native features ship as Kotlin `Plugin` subclasses, which Rust registers through `PluginApi::register_android_plugin` inside a plugin's `setup` hook (`PathPlugin` already works this way). JS talks to these Kotlin plugins through `invoke('plugin:<name>|<cmd>')`, and `addPluginListener` subscribes to events by calling the base `Plugin.registerListener` command, which stores a `Channel` per event name.

This PR connects the core `app` plugin to a new Kotlin `AppPlugin`. When `AppPlugin` is constructed, it adds an `OnBackPressedCallback` to the activity's dispatcher. On each back press it checks `hasListener("back-button")`. With no listener, it navigates the webview back or falls through to the activity's default behaviour. With a listener, it sends `{canGoBack}` to JS. The JS `onBackButtonPress` helper wraps `addPluginListener('app', 'back-button')`. The `register_listener`/`remove_listener` permissions are added to the app plugin's defaults so the webview is allowed to subscribe.
steps: `crates/tauri/src/app/plugin.rs`: the `app` plugin's new `setup` hook calls `register_android_plugin("app.tauri", "AppPlugin")` on Android and stores the handle in managed state.
`crates/tauri/build.rs` plus the autogenerated permissions: `register_listener` and `remove_listener` join the app plugin's default permission set.
`AppPlugin.kt`: the constructor adds an `OnBackPressedCallback`, and `load(webView)` captures the WebView used for `canGoBack`/`goBack`.
`Plugin.kt`: a new `hasListener(event)` helper lets the callback choose between the default behaviour and sending the event to JS.
`TauriActivity.kt`: overrides wry's `handleBackNavigation`, which decides whether wry also handles back presses itself.

findings.title: Android setup block fails to compile: move out of `&PluginHandle`
findings.fixPrompt: In `crates/tauri/src/app/plugin.rs`, the Android-only `setup` block (around lines 135-143) does `let handle_ref = &handle; _app.manage(AppPlugin(*handle_ref));`. `PluginHandle` (crates/tauri/src/plugin.rs ~line 126) is Clone but not Copy, so this is E0507 and Android builds fail. Remove the `handle_ref` indirection and pass `handle` by value to `AppPlugin(handle)`, matching `crates/tauri/src/path/plugin.rs` lines 239-240. If you can, run `cargo check --target aarch64-linux-android -p tauri` to confirm.

findings.title: `handleBackNavigation = true` keeps wry's built-in back handling enabled
findings.fixPrompt: In `crates/tauri/mobile/android-codegen/TauriActivity.kt` line 15, `override val handleBackNavigation: Boolean = true` leaves wry's built-in back navigation enabled. That competes with the new `OnBackPressedCallback` in `crates/tauri/mobile/android/src/main/java/app/tauri/AppPlugin.kt`, so JS `onBackButtonPress` listeners can be bypassed while the webview has history. Change it to `false` so AppPlugin is the only back handler (it already falls back to `webView.goBack()` when no listener exists). Check against wry 0.53.4's `WryActivity` that `false` turns off wry's own handling.

findings.title: Old listeners survive a page reload and leave the back button unresponsive
findings.body:
`handleOnBackPressed` only checks `hasListener(BACK_BUTTON_EVENT)`, which looks at the Kotlin-side `listeners` map:

::diff{file="crates/tauri/mobile/android/src/main/java/app/tauri/AppPlugin.kt" lines="28-46"}

Nothing clears that map when the webview navigates or reloads (a dev reload, `location.reload()`, or an external link). Suppose the page registered `onBackButtonPress` and never called `unregister()`. After a reload, the old channel is still listed. Every back press then goes to a callback that no longer exists, and neither the default `goBack()` nor activity finish runs. To the user, the back button is simply dead.

Other plugins have the same issue with stale listeners, but it hurts more here because this listener suppresses system navigation. One option is to clear `listeners[BACK_BUTTON_EVENT]` on page load. Another is to document that apps must re-register after a reload and accept the risk.
findings.fixPrompt: In `crates/tauri/mobile/android/src/main/java/app/tauri/AppPlugin.kt` (lines 28-46), the back callback suppresses default navigation whenever `hasListener("back-button")` is true. Listeners registered via `Plugin.registerListener` (Plugin.kt) are never cleared on page reload, so after a reload the stale channel swallows every back press. Add cleanup so the back-button listeners are cleared when the webview starts loading a new page (e.g. override a page-load hook available to plugins, or clear the entry when the webview navigates), so the default goBack/finish behaviour comes back until JS registers again.

findings.title: `exit` command is advertised but JS can't call it
findings.body:
Registering a listener turns off the default "finish the activity" behaviour entirely. The app then has to exit by itself when `canGoBack` is `false`. `AppPlugin` defines an `exit` command for this, and the changelog says "support exit and back button press event":

::diff{file="crates/tauri/mobile/android/src/main/java/app/tauri/AppPlugin.kt" lines="49-53"}

However, `exit` is missing from the app plugin's command list in `build.rs`, so it has no permission. There's no Rust command for it either, and `app.ts` has no TS wrapper. In practice, any app using `onBackButtonPress` cannot close itself on the root page without pulling in `plugin-process`.

Either expose it properly (permission entry plus a TS `exit()` that is documented as Android-only), or remove it and point the `onBackButtonPress` docs at `@tauri-apps/plugin-process`'s `exit()`.
findings.fixPrompt: `AppPlugin.kt` (crates/tauri/mobile/android/src/main/java/app/tauri/AppPlugin.kt lines 49-53) defines an `exit` command, but `crates/tauri/build.rs` (app plugin command list ~line 150-170) has no permission for it and `packages/api/src/app.ts` exposes nothing. Apps that register `onBackButtonPress` lose the default activity-finish behaviour and can't exit on their own. Pick one: (a) add an `exit` permission entry in build.rs, regenerate permissions, and add an Android-only `exit()` helper in app.ts; or (b) remove the Kotlin command, update `.changes/android-app-plugin.md`, and document in `onBackButtonPress` JSDoc how to exit (e.g. plugin-process).

findings.title: `onBackButtonPress` docs don't say it only works on Android or that it disables default navigation
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/api/src/app.ts` lines 263-275, expand the JSDoc for `onBackButtonPress`: state that it is Android-only (it rejects on other platforms because `plugin:app|register_listener` doesn't exist there), that registering a listener disables the default goBack/exit behaviour until `unregister()` is called, and add an `@example` that calls `window.history.back()` when `canGoBack` is true. Add an `@since` tag consistent with the other functions in this file.
